grading.gate0: quantities written before the measurement: for session $i$, $K_i$ is the number of other sessions that called between $i$'s two consecutive calls (the LRU stack distance in session units); $i$'s prefix is still cached iff $K_i\,c < C$, with $c$ the context per session; the two branches $$h_{\mathrm{lockstep}}(W/C) = \mathbb{1}\!\left[\tfrac{W}{C} \le 1\right], \qquad h_{\mathrm{dispersed}}(W/C) = \min\!\left(1, \tfrac{C}{W}\right),$$ with $W = N c$ the working set of $N$ sessions. The dispersed formula assumes exponential inter-call times and equal contexts; step 0 replaces both with the recorded distributions. No model sampling (recorded output lengths, content discarded), so no party has a temperature; $K_i$ is read from gateway timestamps and the hit rate from the engine's cached-token counter, not from the formula; goodput is the card's definition with both thresholds visible
grading.gate1: pass: step 0 at $0, step 1 about 65 GPU-h and $200; kill written: step 0 dead if the dispersed-phase replay also predicts a hit rate below 0.4 at the trapped $W/C$ the hardware run reaches; step 1 dead if the jitter, random-order and resident-first arms each leave the hit rate below 0.45 and goodput within 20% of the untreated arm while the arrival cut recovers to within 20% of pre-surge goodput
grading.gate2: route A: the paper states the hysteresis as a fact and attributes it to contents while its model has no state for order; EfficientAgent 2609.33762 writes the dispersed-phase working set in words ('an agent's prefix is reused only if the host tier holds the reusable context of the whole agent pool'); SGLang ships `schedule_policy = 'fcfs'` and switches longest-prefix-match off above 128 waiting requests (source fetched 2026-11-09) — three source types; route B: the ruler $K_i$ with a pre-registered surprise (two branches by phase dispersion against the field's one curve; expected, judgment 0.55: the trapped state has median $K_i/(N-1)$ above 0.9 and the healthy branch below 0.6 at the same $W/C$)
grading.gate3: consumers with actions: SGLang and vLLM maintainers (the prefill scheduling default under backlog), gateway builders (Basin, Continuum, ThunderAgent — ordering before admission), KV working-set planners (an order term), RL-infra teams (MISA-T, TideRL, VenusRL — pace rather than cap concurrency). Community-wide across serving and RL infrastructure — golden-shaped on Gate 3
grading.gate4: mechanism: under a saturated first-come-first-served prefill queue every returning session waits behind every other, so $K_i = N - 1$ for all calls and the cache carries nothing past $W = C$; dispersed phases give $K_i \approx N(1 - e^{-\tau})$ ($\tau$ the session's inter-call time in units of its mean) and a hit rate near $C/W$; consequence: a dispatch-order flag under backlog, or admission as the paper has it
grading.gate5: durable: LRU stack distances (Mattson, Gecsei, Slutz and Traiger 1970) and the convoy phenomenon (Blasgen, Gray, Mitoma and Price 1979) apply to any prefix-cached engine; the SGLang numbers expire with its scheduler; lab-adjacent (systems labs publish measurements; the paper's own group is the natural reviewer)

Medha 2409.17264 uses 'convoy' for head-of-line blocking (a different use); 2606.15555's eviction limit cycle is intra-request
grading.failing_gate: Gate 6 not yet established

headline: On one 8-GPU node, self-GRPO on-policy distillation's reported $50\times$ FLOP saving over GRPO (on-policy distillation: training a student on its own rollouts under a frozen teacher's per-token supervision; FLOPs: floating-point operations) is less than half as large in node-hours (under $25\times$), because the $G = 1$ setting ($G$ rollouts per prompt) buys its FLOPs with eight times the optimizer steps on a decode-bound machine where a batch of 64 and a batch of 512 sequences take nearly the same time to generate.
current_belief: 2611.08453 App. A (card quote): 'Wall-clock and GPU-hours entangle the training objective with implementation and hardware; FLOPs is the only implementation-invariant compute metric'; abstract (fetched 2026-11-09): 'when the teacher is the student's own GRPO checkpoint, OPD recovers that checkpoint's accuracy on math with $50\times$ fewer distillation FLOPs than GRPO needs to reach the same accuracy'; App. I concedes the direction, not the size: the $G = 1$ setting 'takes longer in wall-clock time because it runs more optimizer steps'. The field reads the $50\times$ as a cost ratio a consumer would see (the Thinking Machines post's '7-10x fewer gradient steps => 50-100x compute efficiency').
if_true: FLOP-based efficiency claims for RL and distillation recipes state the batch shape and give node-hours beside FLOPs; the $G = 1$ recipe is retired for single-node users; the lane gets its datum that RL post-training cost on a node is sequential decode steps, not FLOPs, and a two-term cost model (decode steps plus FLOPs) predicts wall-clock across recipes and batch shapes.

headline: Top-$k$ retrieval logs cannot price a memory but can rank one against another, and ranking is all a fixed-size memory store ever does with the price: the expected effect of every same-size swap (replacing one retrieved memory by another at the same $k$) is orthogonal to the kernel that fixed size creates (the directions in value space the log cannot see — a two-line identity), and on the card's own pooled HotpotQA log at least one pairwise contrast (a difference of two memory values) in five among memories retrieved five or more times is determined where one memory value in a thousand is.
current_belief: 2611.03289 abstract (fetched 2026-11-09): 'we prove that top-$k$ retrieval leaves every memory value undetermined, however many episodes are logged'; its remedy LEDGER 'retrieves so that the next log determines more' at 'a cost of 2.6 accuracy points on HotpotQA'; the card's information_asymmetry quotes the paper: 'the history fixes only the differences between values'. CMP 2610.02070 abstract (fetched): 'identified memory utility alone is insufficient for retention decisions'. RoMeRL, Memory-R2 and FadeMem score or learn per-memory values from fixed-size logs as if levels mattered (card neighbours).
if_true: Memory systems keep top-$k$ and lose nothing a retention, merge or retrieval policy can use; the proposed 'fraction of values determined' column becomes the fraction of contrasts determined, or is dropped; LEDGER's 2.6-point price is paid only when the store-size decision is on the table, which is when $k$ varies and the level is identified anyway; for RL memory agents the rewards fix the within-group contrasts GRPO-style objectives use, so the card's 'fixed by the learner and not by the rewards' applies to the level only.
if_false: The kernel under real top-$k$ logs is wide (aliasing of always-co-retrieved pairs, private stores), contrasts are undetermined too, and LEDGER's remedy is necessary for ranking, not only for pricing; or the LEDGER-value ranking retains a better store by at least 3 accuracy points, and the level bought something a store can act on.
probes: C-W45-12 (step 0 $0-10, 2 d: the orthogonality proof for all $|B| < d$ and the kernel of the regenerated plain top-$k$ log at $k = 5$, $T = 7{,}200$, on the card's public setup; step 1 about $20, 3 d: the retention test the card left incomplete — five rankings, keep 30% of the 2,971-memory store, 300 held-out questions, paired per question; 0 GPU-h) — cheapest

grading.gate0: the identity before the estimator: with $(\mathbf{x}_S)_B = \mathbb{1}[B \subseteq S]$ the design row of a retrieved set $S$ and Theorem 1's kernel vectors $\mathbf{h}_B = \sum_{j \notin B} \mathbf{e}_{B \cup \{j\}} - (k - |B|)\,\mathbf{e}_B$ for $|B| < d$ ($d$ the dividend resolution), $$(\mathbf{x}_{S'} - \mathbf{x}_{S})^{\top}\mathbf{h}_B = 0 \quad \text{for every } |B| < d \text{ and every } |S'| = |S| = k.$$ The determined-contrast fraction $F_{\mathrm{pair}}$ is a function of the log's design matrix alone, computed before any outcome is read (the card's kernel test with $\tau = 10^{-8}$); the contrast statement about Shapley values is a $d = 1$ statement, the resolution of every real-data number in the card; aliasing vectors $\mathbf{e}_{\{i\}} - \mathbf{e}_{\{j\}}$ and private-store kernels are not created by fixed size and do void swaps between the aliased pair — $F_{\mathrm{pair}}$ measures how much of the real kernel is $\mathbf{h}_\emptyset$ and how much is these; the reader runs at temperature 0 (zero decision variance by construction) in one launch window, paired per question
grading.gate1: pass: about $30, 0 GPU-h, 5 days; kill written: $F_{\mathrm{pair}}$ under plain top-$k$ below 0.20 while LEDGER's size-varying log gives above 0.60 among the same memories; second kill: the LEDGER-value ranking beats the top-$k$ contrast ranking in retention by at least 3 points with the paired interval excluding zero; pre-registered uninformative reading: all five rankings within 2 points of random at 30% retention voids the retention clause (CMP's finding) while the kernel clause stands or falls on $F_{\mathrm{pair}}$ alone
grading.gate2: route B: the ruler (fraction of pairwise contrasts determined) is computable from any deployed retrieval trace with no outcomes; pre-registered surprise — expected (judgment 0.6) $F_{\mathrm{pair}} \geq 0.6$ against the card's 0.001 for levels; the field assumes the undetermined direction matters (the card's remedy and reporting proposal; RoMeRL's and Memory-R2's learned values); nobody in the fetched set says it is decision-irrelevant
grading.gate3: consumers with actions: memory-system builders (keep top-$k$; drop level-identifying retrieval), memory-benchmark owners (report contrasts determined, or nothing), RL memory-agent authors (read 'fixed by the learner' as a level statement only). One community (agent memory) — proper-shaped, with a general statement (identifiability judged against the decision space) as the ceiling
grading.gate4: mechanism: fixed $k$ confounds the intercept with the sum of values (Scheffé's one-way layout: only contrasts are estimable), and every decision a store makes is a same-size swap whose expected effect is a contrast; consequence: keep top-$k$, or LEDGER's rule is needed for ranking too
grading.gate5: durable: an identity about designs, independent of model, benchmark or memory recipe; lab-adjacent (the card's authors are the natural reviewers and could answer in a v2 — race flag)
grading.gate6: unmeasured: kill search owed (role words: estimable functions, contrasts, identifiability, positivity, Shapley, retention, memory utility, off-policy, slate). headline: A compaction compressor (the model call that summarises an agent's own history to fit its context) at its deployed sampling setting is a gauge, not a function of the history: re-compacting the same pre-compaction history accounts for at least one tenth of the variance of post-compaction harm (TRACE's burden: errored or repeated calls among the next actions), so the one-summary-per-boundary labels the lane builds on — TRACE's paired replay, SJC's 83% entry attribution, the corpus study's history-based triggers — are single readings of an instrument whose repeatability has never been measured.
current_belief: 2610.08722 abstract (fetched 2026-11-09): the best trigger 'reaches held-out AUROC 0.66 (0.64 on the replicate's own label) against a same-boundary replicate of 0.72' — a replicate that, per its App. F (read in full by the import), splits 'each boundary's PRE and POST rollouts into disjoint halves' with the summary held fixed, so it measures the successor stage only; its authors write that 'the same numbers also support an attenuation reading' without a stage split. 2605.23296 abstract (fetched): 'the information it retains fluctuate[s] substantially from run to run, making the agent's retained knowledge unpredictable across runs' — a serving observation with no harm measurement. TRACE, SJC, HSC-Bench and 2611.06545 each use one summary per boundary.
if_true: Compaction evaluations add a writer-replicate arm ($m \geq 3$ re-compactions per boundary) beside the successor replicate and report the nested variance components; per-boundary harm labels and SJC's per-entry attribution are read as one draw; history-based triggers are read against the reliability ceiling $\rho_1 = \sigma^2_B / (\sigma^2_B + \sigma^2_W + \sigma^2_E / n)$ ($n$ continuations per summary; symbols defined in gate0); CL-W44-06's census and deletion arms average over writer draws; harness teams run the compressor at temperature 0 or ensemble $m$ draws if the share is high.
if_false: The compressor is effectively deterministic at the deployed setting (writer share under 0.10), single-summary labels are licensed, TRACE's successor-only replicate is the right yardstick, and the result is a protocol footnote; if the per-writer unsupported-policy rate is stable across re-compactions it is a calibratable writer bias (a column per writer model), not dice.
probes: import:2026-W45-S3xF9 (steps 1-3 about 30 GPU-h, about $100, 10 d on 2611.06545's released handoff-audit harness: 150 compaction boundaries x 4 re-compactions at the deployed temperature x 3 continuations of 8 successor steps, judge-free harm, nested ANOVA with a boundary-cluster bootstrap, a temperature-0 control arm, a second writer; optional AppWorld replication in SJC's harness about $400) — cheapest

grading.gate0: nested model written first: $y_{bjk} = \mu + \alpha_b + \beta_{j(b)} + \epsilon_{k(bj)}$ for boundary $b$, re-compaction $j$ and continuation $k$, with variance components $\sigma^2_B$ (between histories), $\sigma^2_W$ (writer: between summaries of one history) and $\sigma^2_E$ (successor: between continuations of one summary); the headline quantity is the writer share $\sigma^2_W / (\sigma^2_B + \sigma^2_W + \sigma^2_E)$. Whose temperature: the writer's is stated (Qwen3-8B at 0.6, gpt-oss-20b at 1.0, the developers' settings) and a temperature-0 control arm separates sampling variance from serving nondeterminism; harm is judge-free (TRACE burden; 2611.06545's ledger-checked unsupported action); the replay certificate of 2611.05650 is required — dead as a ruler if fewer than 100 of 150 snapshots re-execute to an identical state
grading.gate1: pass: about 30 GPU-h and $100, 10 days; kill written: writer share under 0.10 with the bootstrap interval's upper end under 0.20 on both writers
grading.gate2: route B: a ruler (the nested components and the reliability ceiling) with a pre-registered surprise — expected (judgment 0.45) a writer share of at least 0.25, 0.3 that it lies between 0.10 and 0.25, 0.25 that it is under 0.10 — against the field's one-summary-per-boundary practice; the corpus study's own authors name the attenuation reading and do not split the stages

headline: Only one or two numbers per scene are worth measuring, and which ones can be computed in simulation before any robot time: the value of calibrating each physical parameter under a material prior is concentrated in task-specific parameters, and for most tabletop tasks it is below the cost of measuring, so a material-prior database plus randomization is the right default and targeted calibration the exception.
raised_by: Jacob and a colleague, 2026-11-03: collaborators say per-scene physical-parameter calibration by a VLM-driven real robot is 'heavily adopted' in real-to-sim data-synthesis pipelines; their prior is that a database of material-parameter confidence intervals plus domain randomization suffices. Investigation of the seven real-to-sim questions in data/threads/PROGRAM-L5-simulators.md Part V.
current_belief: Two camps, neither with a per-parameter number. Measure: 2606.22062 (sim-to-sim pendulum, two parameters: 'a small number of identification rollouts closed most of the transfer gap ... broad randomization that contained the true system still did not substitute for measurement'), Phys2Real 2510.11689 (VLM prior + online estimate beats DR 100 vs 79 and 57 vs 23 on CoM-offset pushing), ForceTwin 2609.21751 (probed mechanisms 87 vs 60 over a VLM prior), 2503.01255 (static joint friction left out of DR broke transfer). Randomize: Digital Cousins 2410.07408 (twins 'cannot produce cross-domain generalization'), co-training recipe 2503.24361 (+38 percent 'even with notable differences between the simulation and real-world data'), MetaGenSim 2610.19479 (optimises the generation distribution and 'matches expert manual alignment' with no alignment), InternData-A1 2511.16651 (synthetic-only pre-training matches the pi dataset), AutoRSR 2610.20336 (73-87 percent real success from randomized synthetic episodes). Pipelines that calibrate choose the parameters by VLM semantics (2601.08454: 'the minimal subset of missing physical parameters required for the simulation task'). In a 75-paper agent x real2sim2real list (2026-07-19 to 10-16) one paper (D-World) has an agent revise physical parameters on a real robot; about 16 identify parameters without an agent (deformables, tactile, actuators); about 24 are geometry only. Industry assigns, it does not measure (NVIDIA SimReady blog: friction 'assumed 0.8 / 0.6 ... not calibrated against physical measurements').
if_true: Real-to-sim pipelines run a simulated pre-flight check - the per-parameter value table under the scene's material prior - and spend robot time only on the one or two parameters above their measurement cost; a material-prior database becomes a first-class artefact; evaluation twins keep full calibration (where the sim must predict this scene) and training data keeps breadth (cousins); the collaborators' prior is confirmed for most tasks and bounded for the CoM / mechanism / static-friction class.
if_false: Either the value is spread across many parameters (then the only question is the budget split of 2606.22062 and 'targeted' is empty), or targeted calibration never beats a widened prior at any budget (then randomization is right everywhere and the result is a confirmation table), or a per-parameter value rule is already in print at full-text reading.
probes: P-W45-J01-a (open, design owed; 40-60 GPU-h, $80-180, 3 weeks): the value spectrum - for six tabletop tasks in MJX/Genesis, one mask-conditioned policy per task trained under a material prior; reveal one parameter at a time and read the success gain; report the per-parameter value, its concentration, and the Sobol index of the randomized policy's success

P-W45-J01-a.what: Tasks (MuJoCo Playground / ManiSkill / Genesis): CoM-offset T-block push (Phys2Real's class), box pick-and-place, spring-and-damper drawer opening (ForceTwin's class), peg insertion, Leap in-hand cube reorientation, and one deformable (cloth fold in Genesis) if time allows. Parameters per scene: object-table friction, object-gripper friction, mass, centre-of-mass offset, restitution, joint stiffness and damping, actuator gain scale (and cloth stiffness). Material prior: log-uniform within handbook ranges, the arm the collaborators propose. Train one policy per task and seed conditioned on a masked parameter vector (masked entries replaced by the prior mean; masks random during training so every conditioning pattern is in-distribution). Evaluate across the prior with nothing revealed (J_0), one parameter revealed (J_k), everything revealed (J_all). Report EVPI_k = J_k - J_0, total J_all - J_0, concentration max_k EVPI_k / total, and the Sobol index S_k of the no-reveal policy's success. Two engines so the numbers are not one engine's contact model.

Expected (judgment): total value under 5 points on pick-and-place and peg insertion, 15-40 points on CoM-offset pushing and the spring drawer, top parameter above 60 percent of total in at least five of six tasks. neighbors.title: Prorsa: Unleashing the Potential of Prefill-Decode Disaggregation in Agentic Reinforcement Learning
neighbors.trick: Watch every trajectory's stage to forecast ten seconds of prefill tokens and decode KV, then flip rollout engines between prefill and decode roles.
neighbors.difference: none for the mechanism half — occupied: §5.2 attributes the math/agentic sign reversal to 'much less overlap between prefill and decode'; Fig. 1 gives the temporal profile across staleness 0/2/8. Lacks a log statistic and the crossing of overlap with prefill-token share; its async math still re-prefills at step start.

neighbors.title: AInfer-PD: Communication-Safe In-Place Prefill-Decode Multiplexing for Distributed MoE Rollouts
neighbors.trick: Keep prefill and decode on the same MoE devices and KV store but order their collectives across ranks and separate DeepEP's path state so they run concurrently.
neighbors.difference: States the overlap rule for the in-place alternative ('P/D coexistence a persistent property of the rollout'; 'Longer client waits leave less overlap opportunity'; activation 'only when concurrent P work exists'); no log statistic, no disaggregated arm.

neighbors.title: PEARL: Adaptive Prefill-Decode Execution with Elasticity for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
neighbors.trick: Fit closed-form colocated and disaggregated makespan models from telemetry, enumerate PD ratios under the GPU budget, pick the lowest predicted makespan with hysteresis.
neighbors.difference: Occupies the ruler form with a different statistic: f = average fraction of trajectories actively decoding, theta=(1-f)/f; colocation modelled additively with work conservation (no interference term), so Omega is absent. Measured reversal: +9.7% at BS32 to a 6.1% colocation win at BS96. The record's 'profiling, not a statistic' was wrong.

neighbors.title: When Cache Pressure Becomes a Trap: Metastability in Agent Serving
neighbors.trick: Count every active session's context, tool-idle included, as the prefix-cache working set; past ~1.9x capacity the engine stays trapped after a surge.
neighbors.difference: Second regime rule for PD topology, eq. 2: cache-first when C <~ D_KV/(2f), f the fraction of sessions in service; tool time enters through f, not turn count; in 1P3D agent serving the prefix cache binds before interference. Colocated engines left open (§9).

neighbors.title: Observation, Not Prediction: Conversation-Level Disaggregated Scheduling for Agentic Serving

neighbors.difference: Already dethrones the turn as the unit of the disaggregation decision ('imposed by the scheduling unit, not the workload'); serving, no statistic.

neighbors.title: Crossflow: Prefill-Decode Elasticity for Agentic LLM Serving
neighbors.trick: Decode nodes publish revocable leases to run some prefill locally so the P/D boundary flexes.
neighbors.difference: The shipped workload descriptor for P/D sizing is the uncached-input-to-output token ratio (a volume ratio, not temporal overlap); any Omega paper must beat it.

kill_search.summary: Killed at Gate 2B. The mechanism half of the headline is the source paper's own sentence: Prorsa (2610.16592; trick: watch every trajectory's stage to forecast ten seconds of prefill tokens and decode KV, then flip rollout engines between prefill and decode roles) writes in §5.2 'In contrast, on the math task, normalized rollout step times range from 0.86 to 1.28 relative to colocation, indicating a slowdown in most evaluated settings. This is due to much less overlap between prefill and decode: rollout first prefills all sequences and then executes successive decoding steps.' AInfer-PD (2609.00993; trick: keep prefill and decode on the same MoE devices and KV store but order their collectives across ranks so they run concurrently) states the same rule for the in-place alternative — 'making P/D coexistence a persistent property of the rollout rather than a one-time prompt-ingestion event' — and its limitations say 'Disaggregation remains preferable when separate phase capacity and KV transfer are acceptable' and 'broader scales and hardware remain open'. No fetched paper asserts turn count as the rule (ConServe 2606.01839 already removes the turn as the decision unit), so the contrast has no believer. The ruler form is shipped by PEARL (2609.35158: closed-form makespan models on the fraction of trajectories actively decoding, f) and, for serving, Basin 2611.02543 eq. 2 ($C \lesssim D_{\mathrm{KV}}/(2f)$); 2611.05991 settles only that chunked-prefill defaults confound engine comparisons (78% of the capacity gap). Residue: the unrun crossing control — at matched prefill-token share, phase-locked turns remove at least half of the disaggregation speedup — footnote-grade, ~40 GPU-h.

kill_search.summary: Killed at concept level (2026-11-08): the claim's first clause was published with full-history controls by two groups within three days of filing. ARCBench 2611.03223 (2026-11-02) — inside the pi harness, give the agent a rule and a history, compact it or keep it whole, issue a forbidden request, grade the tool call, and label whether the summary kept the rule and why the agent broke a rule it still had — finds 'compaction rarely deletes the rule: most violations after compaction occur while the rule is still in the compacted history, with the agent treating a later request as permission' (retained 70.1% / partially 26.9% / absent 3.0% of compacted runs; retained-rule runs violate 21.1% vs 8.1% with full history), and leaves open 'explain why agents still violate retained rules ... longer sessions with repeated compaction'. Handoff-audit 2611.06545 (2026-11-04) — a per-task permission ledger plus same-snapshot replay with the flagged sentence swapped for filler — finds 59 of 76 held-out unsupported restrictions overgeneralized (lost target binding) and 39 of 42 authorizations stale or look-alike, and concedes 'the full-history arm changes both the content and the length of the successor's context' and 'Templates that vary the two independently would be needed'; its count-matched control edit (25 of 120 vs 7 of 120 unauthorized actions, post hoc) is the first length control on deleting unsourced entries and runs against the claim's second clause. 2611.05650 adds that the census probe is a transcript label that 'cannot distinguish a cause of failure from something that co-occurs with it'. Residue (new claim, proper-shaped, ARCBench authors are the race): the retained-rule excess closes by restoring one record of the agent's own earlier compliance at matched tokens, not by restating the rule.

kill_search.summary: Killed at Gate 2B. The two-arm comparison the claim needs was run as an audit paragraph in The Replay Gap (2608.08239, 2026-08-08): fork live SWE-bench trajectories, rebuild the container by re-executing the recorded commands, and continue with the same model as a control that 'absorbs sampler nondeterminism, batching effects, and environment-replay drift'; under identical temperature-0 decoding, AWQ-served controls 'half never diverge at any action' while FP8-served controls 'diverge on 90-96% of forks', with environment reconstruction verified at 99.99% return-code agreement over 11,702 replayed actions, so the serving path alone moves the diverging share by 40-45 points and the environment's command-level channel is near zero; its limitation names only 'unquantized pools and a third fork position' as next steps. The serving channel's outcome magnitude comes from 2607.09691 (2026-06-19): one temperature-0 API call per instance, a deterministic patch builder and the official Docker grader, and still '6/70 flips' (about 9%) between byte-identical runs, 'a caution that applies to single-run SWE-bench comparisons generally'; the environment channel's magnitude from Anthropic's 2026-02-05 post is the infra-error rate 'from 5.8% at strict enforcement to 0.5% when uncapped' (2.1% at 3x headroom), with the timing channel 'not formally quantified'. On the suites the claim names the serving channel is three to four times the environment's, so the field's attribution (HAL sec. 4) stands as the majority reading; the second-sampling-party clause is an unpinned-simulator protocol defect already held by C-W44-OWN-2 (lab-parked). No residue claim; C-W44-07 and C-W45-04 die with the claim, C-W45-04's certificate cell belongs under CL-W44-06.

neighbors.title: When the Simulator Fails, Not the Policy: Auditing Contact Artifacts in Simulated Robot Benchmarks (SimuGuard)

headline: On HAL's tau-bench airline cells under the Generalist scaffold, more than one in five of the task-level disagreements between two archived runs of the same model is a trigger flip (the grader ran in one run and not in the other), not the agent solving the task in one run and failing in the other, so the replicate disagreement and pass^k (the chance that all $k$ runs of a task pass) those cells report measure the instrument's trigger before they measure the agent.

if_true: Benchmark owners that grade on an ending event (tau-bench, tau2-bench, HAL's airline cells) report pass^k with the grading rate and split replicate disagreement into trigger flips and outcome flips; the remedy for the Generalist's deficit is a grading rule that fires on agent exit (or a resume step), not the paper's reporting column alone; 2611.04399's per-model 'bias' directions are re-read as means of a noisy indicator; CL-W44-07's 'second sampling party' clause gets its measurement-event mechanism.

grading.gate0: quantities defined on the probe record: published disagreement $D_{\mathrm{pub}} = \frac{1}{n}\sum_i \mathbb{1}[r_{i1} \neq r_{i2}]$ over $n = 41$ tasks with stored rewards $r_{ir} \in \{0,1\}$; trigger share $\tau$ = disagreements with $G_{i1} \neq G_{i2}$ over all disagreements, $G_{ir} \in \{0,1\}$ the grading indicator (a function of the stored record: an injected gold copy or a positive reward); $J$ the Jaccard overlap of the two ungraded sets; $D_{\mathrm{all}}$ the disagreement after offline re-grading. Conditioning set: the archive's recorded sampling setting, read at step 0 — if above temperature 0 the agent's sampling enters and the record says so; at temperature 0 a trigger flip is serving or simulator arithmetic reaching the stop rule. Grader (the tau-bench database rule) and second party (the user simulator) are kept distinct.
grading.gate1: pass: C-W45-01 steps 0-1 at $0 and 0 GPU-h, 5 days; kill written: $J \geq 0.75$ and $\tau \leq 0.2$ (bootstrap upper bound under 0.35) pooled over Generalist two-run cells, so that $D_{\mathrm{pub}}/D_{\mathrm{all}} \leq 1.1$; also dead if step 0 finds the ungraded episodes carry a terminating event the paper's rule missed
grading.gate2: route B: the ruler (trigger share $\tau$ of replicate disagreement) is identifiable from the archive, computable from data HAL holds, with a pre-registered surprise — expected (judgment 0.5) $\tau \geq 0.4$ and $J \in [0.3, 0.6]$ on Generalist cells, $\tau \approx 0$ on Tool-Calling cells (graded 98%); the field assumes $\tau \approx 0$ (HAL's serving attribution; 2609.37315's 'present on every rerun')
grading.gate3: three consumer classes with actions: benchmark owners (grade on agent exit; publish the grading rate beside pass^k), leaderboard operators (split replicate disagreement into trigger and outcome flips), auditors who re-grade from logs (resume the second party before grading — the orphan C-W45-02's question). Population: every leaderboard that reports pass^k on a user-simulator benchmark — one community; proper-shaped unless termination-gated graders prove common on other benchmark families

headline: 'Repaired' is a maintainer's convention, not a state of the task: on the Terminal-Bench 2.0 tasks whose instruction-test mismatch was fixed twice — Z.ai's Verified tightened the instruction, Terminal-Bench 2.1 loosened the test — the two repairs lift different agents, with the top-band minus mid-band gain (the two strongest probed models' gain minus the two middle ones') positive under the loosened test and negative under the tightened instruction, each outside the five-trial replicate interval.
current_belief: 2611.08417 App. A.3 (card quote): 'when an instruction and its test disagree, Verified edits the instruction to state what the test checks, whereas Terminal-Bench 2.1 more often edits the test to accept any correct solution; stating the grader's expectation tells the agent part of the solution, while relaxing the grader leaves the task as hard as its contributor intended' — read by the paper as restoring the intended task; its abstract (fetched 2026-11-09) reads the 2.1 repairs as removed defects: 'accuracy increased by over 10 percentage points and leaderboard positions move by up to three ranks'. ABA 2605.26079 takes the maintainers' fix PR as the unique ground truth for 'broken'.
if_true: Continuous benchmarks publish the repair convention per task (tighten / loosen / environment) and the inter-repair delta beside the version delta; audit tools that propose repairs (ABA, the 2611.08417 workflow) report the convention they chose; CL-W44-11's content-repaired set is split by convention before any repair share is read; a lab's launch table citing a version is read with its repairs' band signature.
if_false: Two independent repairs of an instruction-test mismatch are interchangeable to within replicate noise: 'repaired' is a well-defined state of the task, the version delta is a property of the defect, audit workflows may pick the cheaper fix — which strengthens 2611.08417's paired re-score and the difference-in-differences design on 3.0 to 4.0.

kill_search.summary: Killed at claim level. The two repairs are not independent: the Terminal-Bench 2.1 README (PR #53) says 'many were taken directly from Z.ai's Terminal-Bench 2.0 Verified changes' and Z.ai's card calls 2.1 a collaboration ('jointly reviewing tasks, validating fixes'); the file diff shows 2.1 adopted Verified's tightening on 4 of the 11 shared tasks, leaving 3 clean divergences (hf-model-inference, train-fasttext, polyglot-c-py), two of them without headroom in the paper's own Table 7 (88.3% to 86.7%; 5.0% to 3.3%), so the probe parks at its own step 0. Closest paper 1, 2611.08417 (repair 28 TB 2.0 tasks under a rubric, re-score 19 agents on both versions, state the two conventions in prose): 'when an instruction and its test disagree, Verified edits the instruction to state what the test checks, whereas Terminal-Bench 2.1 more often edits the test to accept any correct solution; stating the grader's expectation tells the agent part of the solution, while relaxing the grader leaves the task as hard as its contributor intended' and 'Agreement measures consistency rather than correctness.' Closest paper 2, 2610.22760 (vary the specification level of coding tasks for three models under one harness): 'additional reference-derived descriptions can improve resolution, but their benefit is not consistent across models' and, in Limitations, 'Budget constraints limited each reported configuration to one trajectory per instance, making small differences sensitive to stochastic variation.' SWE-Bench Pro V2 (2610.24206) states the opposite convention as a lesson ('weakening a test to fit an instruction changes what the benchmark measures'), so the claim's surprise is the field's stated knowledge (Gate 2B). Residue (new claim): the SWE-Bench Pro tasks repaired by both Pro Verified and Pro V2, compared on agent ordering against a matched random-subset ceiling.

headline: The reported collapse of multi-turn RL to or below its base model at a quarter of the turn cap is a budget-prompt effect, not a budget dependence of what RL learned: on FrozenLake with the prompt's budget line held at $T_{\max}$ (the full cap) and success read at one attempt, the RL model stays above the base model at 25% of the cap.
current_belief: 2611.06483 abstract (fetched 2026-11-09): 'we show that trajectory-level RL advantages depend on sufficient turn budgets, diminishing significantly when budgets tighten'; sec. 3.2 (card): 'These results suggest that the gains of agentic RL depend on a sufficient interaction budget'; App. B.3: 'We conjecture that agent RL primarily strengthens long-horizon capabilities whose benefits emerge when sufficient interaction budget is available'. The protocol: 'The budget is specified in the system prompt before generation begins' (App. B.1) and 'we fix the sampling breadth at $k=8$ and vary the maximum interaction turns $T$' (sec. 3.2).
if_true: Budget sweeps hold the prompt and report $\mathrm{Pass}@(1,T)$ (success at one attempt under cap $T$) beside $\mathrm{Pass}@(8,T)$; the deployment-risk warning reverses (an RL agent under a silent cap is fine, under an announced unfamiliar cap it is not); BudgetMix's +7.5 points at 25% is read as partly prompt-distribution matching, which a one-line prompt-mixing control also buys; the Pass@(k,T) family (2604.14877) reports the no-counter curve.
if_false: The sweep is a true budget dependence: the RL model's full-cap successes concentrate beyond the 25% cut; the fix belongs in training (budget sampling or a turns-used term) and the next probe is the training 2x2 the card names (BudgetMix vs a turns-used reward vs budget-blind RL); the orphan import S8xF4's terminal-value reading becomes the live alternative mechanism.
probes: import:2026-W45-S8xF9 (one Full-budget GRPO run on FrozenLake plus inference, about 50 GPU-h, $150-250 at spot rates, 10 d: the prompt gap $\Delta_\pi(T)$ between running under cap $T$ with the counter in the prompt and reading the full-budget success curve at $T$, plus the success / wrong-commit / still-running split) — cheapest

C-W45-06 (about 110 GPU-h standalone, about 30 GPU-h beyond S8xF9's training run, $0 on owned GPUs, 10 d: the 2x2 of announced vs held prompt by $K = 8$ vs $K = 1$ at four caps, with the truncation identity check and the turns-to-success distributions)
source: lifted from C-W45-06 and import S8xF9 (card 2611.06483); the three W45 L2 protocol candidates shared a three-clause headline_test and are filed as three one-quantifier claims (this one, CL-W45-04, and CL-W45-06 in L3) per the 2026-11-01 conjunction lesson

grading.gate0: FrozenLake transitions are deterministic ('known deterministic transition dynamics', App. B.4), so there is no luck term after the action; the quantity $p_T(x) = \Pr_{\tau \sim \pi(\cdot \mid x, T_{\max})}[R(\tau) = 1,\ \ell(\tau) \leq T]$ ($x$ the task, $R \in \{0,1\}$ the terminal verifier, $\ell(\tau)$ the turns the trajectory used) is a property of the (policy, prompt, cap) triple and the headline names all three; whose temperature: the $K = 8$ coverage term belongs to the sampled policy at 0.6, and the base is flatter than the RL model (card: cumulative log-likelihood ratio about 228 vs 26), so $K = 1$ and $K = 8$ are reported side by side and step 3 repeats at 1.0; the structural upper bound (shortest path per map) is overlaid so a map unsolvable at 25% is not read as a policy failure
grading.gate1: pass: S8xF9 at about 50 GPU-h (one GRPO training run is unavoidable: 'Model weights ... are not bundled', README); kill written: at 25% of cap $|\Delta_{\mathrm{RL}}| < 3$ points with the interval excluding $-5$ and the RL-minus-base deficit mostly wrong commits (S8xF9), or the held-prompt $K = 1$ gap at 25% at or below zero with its band excluding half the full-cap lead (C-W45-06)
grading.gate2: route B: the ruler is the paper's own sweep with the prompt held, read at $K = 1$, with a pre-registered surprise — expected (judgment 0.55): the announced $K = 8$ reading reproduces the paper and the held $K = 1$ reading leaves RL above base at 25%; the field reads the sweep as a property of the policy (2604.14877 and the card's sec. 3.2 sentence)
grading.gate3: consumers with actions: multi-turn RL evaluators (hold the prompt; report $\mathrm{Pass}@(1,T)$ with the cap drawn as a censoring line), BudgetMix adopters (run the prompt-mixing control), deployers under step caps (drop the counter rather than retrain), RL framework maintainers (log termination type and turn per rollout). Population: everyone evaluating RL'd agents under a turn cap — one community (agent-RL evaluation), proper-shaped
grading.gate4: mechanism: a tight-budget evaluation under the paper's protocol is a prompt the RL model never trained on and a cut it was never scored under, at once, while the base model saw neither prompt; the eight-try coverage bonus of the flatter base adds a second term; consequence: prompt-held $K = 1$ sweeps become the reading rule, or the training 2x2 runs
grading.gate5: a reading rule for any budget sweep (durable while Pass@(k,T) sweeps are the lane's standard); the FrozenLake number itself expires with the paper's v2; lab-adjacent (a control, not a recipe); race flag: the paper's authors can run it in a day on their checkpoints
grading.gate6: unmeasured: kill search owed (role words: budget-aware prompt, turn budget, interaction budget, remaining turns, anytime, truncation, censoring, competing risks, Pass@(k,T), horizon cap). Nearest: 2604.14877 (fetched 2026-11-09: 'PASS@(k,T), a two-dimensional metric that jointly varies sampling budget k and interaction depth T'; its prompt handling unread), DAPRO 2605.06605 and HARP 2610.07362 (cap as censoring for evaluation-budget allocation, one event type), AnySearch 2609.00813 and On the Clock 2610.10833 (budget-aware training — the time-awareness route), 2412.18547 (budget in the prompt, single-turn). The step-0 letter to the authors for the checkpoint is also the re-open test
grading.failing_gate: none hard; Gate 4 mechanism rewrite owed (why GRPO-Full and not GiGPO/PPO-Full); Gate 6 race flag (authors' v2); 2026-11-01 conjunction lesson (two one-quantifier claims)
grading.rank_reason_w45: the first live L2 claim since W43 with a probe under one GPU-week; reverses a reading stated in print; one community; race with the authors' v2; ranked above its sibling CL-W45-04 because the cheaper probe reads a published headline directly
grading.kill_verdict_w45: No occupant of the announced-vs-held control on a fixed-cap RL checkpoint and the paper never runs it (Gate 0/2B question answered no); survival is weak because the paper's own GiGPO/PPO cells show the announced prompt is not sufficient for collapse and AdaTurn Table 1 shows a silent-cap collapse of a budget-blind RL agent (judgment probability of the expected result 0.55 -> 0.25), the headline bundles a prompt term and a coverage term (split into CL-W45-03a/b), and the race is with three groups holding the stack.

scorecard.target_value: In print: the paper's own protocol sentences and its admission that the two readings are entangled by design ('Full-Budget and BudgetMix RL use identical training settings; their only difference is the distribution of budgets', App. A.2); 2604.14877 introduced $\mathrm{Pass}@(k,T)$ 'to characterize multi-turn capability boundaries'. Who pays: anyone evaluating an RL-trained agent under a turn or step cap (BFCL, Terminal-Bench, tool-call limits), teams about to adopt BudgetMix, and the Pass@(k,T) authors whose metric is being read as a policy property.

kill_search.summary: The claim survives weakly: nobody has evaluated a fixed-cap RL checkpoint at a tight cap with the counter announced versus held, and the card paper never does (2611.06483: 'The budget is specified in the system prompt before generation begins', App. B.1; 'we inform the model of the total budget limit and the remaining budget within the prompt', sec. 5.4; repository: 'budget-visible rerolls'). Closest, 2604.14877 (Pass@(k,T): 64 separate rollouts per depth with a prompt that never mentions T) is the silent-cap sweep in another domain and finds no collapse — RL-minus-base about -3 at k=1 and +4 at k=64 at both T=1 and T=5 — with its own limitation 'did not evaluate at interaction depths beyond the training budget ... the temperature sweep, which controls for the possibility that RL training mechanically lowers the output entropy and thereby inflates PASS@(1,T) while deflating PASS@(64,T), are the most important next runs'. Second, AdaTurn 2607.14547 (condition a visual agent on the allowed turns and train the final-turn boundary as a forced answer) shows the silent-cap collapse of a budget-blind RL agent — 'Mini-o3's performance on VisualProbe-Hard benchmark reduces from 48.0% to 26.5% after we limit the maximum rollout turns to 4' — and names the mechanism 'catastrophic truncation'; its Limitations: 'Our study is restricted to image-based agents and does not cover video settings'. Inside the card paper, GiGPO-Full and PPO-Full under the same announced protocol keep their FrozenLake lead at 25% ('rather than losing their advantage as the budget tightens, models trained with these algorithms achieve relatively consistent gains across budgets', App. D.1), so the prompt is not sufficient for collapse. The headline is split into a prompt-term claim (03a) and a coverage-term claim (03b); S8xF9 and C-W45-06 survive with redesigns; the race is with the authors' v2.

headline: The verdict that multi-turn RL improves single-step decision quality on fewer than half of states is a ruler choice: on FrozenLake, judged by the base policy's own continuation on the ordinary states the RL policy actually visits, the RL action is the better one on more than half of them.
current_belief: 2611.06483 abstract (fetched 2026-11-09): 'agentic RL does not uniformly elevate single-step decision quality; rather, its strength concentrates in error recovery and long-horizon resilience'; sec. 3.3 (card): 'RL achieves better step-level decision quality on only 46.8% of DeepCoder-MT states and 42.8% of FrozenLake states, with average quality no better than, even slightly below, the base model', graded against 'the exact $Q^{*}$ value of each step-level action under optimal continuation within the remaining interaction budget' on a pool sampled 'equally from base and RL trajectories'.
if_true: Every step-quality claim names the continuation policy and the state weights and reports the identity check; the 'RL does not improve per-step actions' story and the remedies built on it (process rewards, step judges) are re-read; the $R_{\mathrm{single}}$ decline on a fixed base-state pool is a visitation shift, not a loss of step quality.
if_false: Recovery-after-error is confirmed under the right ruler: more than 70% of the summed advantage sits on post-error histories and the win share stays below 52%; the paper's reading gains the identity it lacked and the next step-grading paper cites the identity check as a method note.

grading.gate0: the quantity is written before the estimator — the performance difference lemma (Kakade and Langford 2002) for a finite horizon, discount 1, deterministic environment: $$J(\pi_{\mathrm{RL}}) - J(\pi_{\mathrm{B}}) = \sum_{t=1}^{T_{\max}} \mathbb{E}_{h_t \sim d_t^{\pi_{\mathrm{RL}}},\ a_t \sim \pi_{\mathrm{RL}}(\cdot \mid h_t)} \bigl[ Q^{\pi_{\mathrm{B}}}(h_t, a_t) - V^{\pi_{\mathrm{B}}}(h_t) \bigr],$$ with $J(\pi)$ the success probability of policy $\pi$, $d_t^{\pi}$ the distribution of histories at turn $t$ under $\pi$, $Q^{\pi_{\mathrm{B}}}(h, a)$ the success probability of taking $a$ at $h$ and following the base policy after, and $V^{\pi_{\mathrm{B}}}(h)$ its average over the base's own actions. The paper's ruler replaces $Q^{\pi_{\mathrm{B}}}$ by $Q^{*}$ and $d^{\pi_{\mathrm{RL}}}$ by a half-and-half pool. FrozenLake is deterministic, so there is no luck term after the action; whose temperature: $Q^{\pi_{\mathrm{B}}}$ is a property of the base at the stated 0.6 and is repeated at 1.0; 'error state' is the paper's injected proxy ('proxies rather than rigorous definitions of error states', App. B.5) and is kept as its own stratum
grading.gate1: pass: about 30 GPU-h marginal on the shared checkpoint; kill written: the RL win share under $Q^{\pi_{\mathrm{B}}}$ on RL-visited ordinary histories below 52% (bootstrap band over 200 histories) with the identity check passing (summed advantage within 3 points of the measured $\mathrm{Pass}@1$ gain) and more than 70% of the sum on post-error histories
grading.gate2: route B: a ruler with an identity behind it and a pre-registered surprise — expected (judgment 0.55) RL wins 60-70% of RL-visited ordinary histories under $Q^{\pi_{\mathrm{B}}}$ against the paper's 42.8% under $Q^{*}$ on the symmetric pool; the field reads matched-state grading under $Q^{*}$ as a property of the policy
grading.gate3: consumers with actions: step-grading and process-reward authors (name the continuation policy and the state weights), critic papers (the identity check as a method note), training teams choosing between outcome RL and process supervision on the strength of such readings. One community (the step-credit lane) — proper-shaped
grading.gate4: mechanism: what GRPO learns on a grid is to stop walking into regions where the base falls into holes, which $Q^{*}$ under optimal continuation barely penalises and $Q^{\pi_{\mathrm{B}}}$ penalises fully; a half-and-half pool graded by a perfect player measures the perfect player's map, not the difference between the two agents; consequence: the reading rule, or the confirmation of recovery
grading.gate5: durable: the identity applies to any policy pair and any environment; the FrozenLake number expires with the paper's v2; lab-adjacent (a ruler, not a recipe); the authors hold the checkpoints
grading.gate6: unmeasured: kill search owed (role words: matched states, step-level action quality, continuation, state visitation, performance difference, advantage decomposition, error recovery). The arXiv abstract conjunction 'performance difference lemma' AND (language model OR LLM) returned 0 on 2026-11-09 — a density datum, to be re-run in the neighbours' words (checklist 2026-10-25); Probe-and-Resume 2610.21088 grades critics against executed continuations and GiGPO 2505.10978 groups anchor states; pre-window precedents CPI 2002 and TRPO 2015 use the identity for training, never for reading an agent
grading.failing_gate: Gate 2B (pre-registered surprise equals the field's stated knowledge); Gate 6 why-now 'no reason found'
grading.rank_reason_w45: an identity-backed ruler that reverses a stated verdict at 30 GPU-h on a shared checkpoint; one community; Jacob's edge direct
grading.kill_verdict_w45: Gate 2B: the ruler-dependence of step quality is PAV 2410.08146's theorem and mechanism sentence (Lemma F.1 is the performance difference lemma), the state-weight half is stated for LLM RL by 2609.39634, and the expected result ('RL wins on the states it steers into under the base's continuation') is 2611.06483's own reading ('long-horizon execution and error recovery') in other words — the authors would call it a confirmation, not a reversal; why-not-done is 'no reason found'.

Who pays: anyone grading an RL'd agent step by step (process-reward builders, critic papers, the paper's authors), and training teams deciding between outcome RL and process supervision on such readings.

impact_ceiling.floor: A method note: the identity check and the two-ruler table on FrozenLake, cited by the paper's v2 and the next matched-state analysis; needs step 2. Judgment p 0.5.
impact_ceiling.middle: A reading rule for step-quality claims (name the continuation policy and the state weights; report the identity check) adopted by the step-credit lane's next two papers, plus the DeepCoder-MT extension. Judgment p 0.3.
impact_ceiling.ceiling: The decomposition of multi-turn RL's gain by depth, state stratum and continuation becomes the lane's ruler for 'what RL changed'; the $R_{\mathrm{single}}$ reading is retired; with CL-W45-03 the L2 program stands. Judgment p 0.1.

headline: The post-surge hit-rate deficit of a prefix cache (the reuse of a prompt's already-computed attention states) serving agent sessions at equal working set (the aggregate context of the active sessions) is a convoy, not a cache-contents effect: the prefill queue has locked the sessions' call phases together so every returning prefix finds the whole population ahead of it, and a dispatch-order change at unchanged arrivals (random order, or resident-first) lifts the hit rate back above 0.45 within ten minutes where the paper's only recovery lever was cutting arrivals.
current_belief: 2611.02543 sec. 5.2 (card quote): 'This is cache hysteresis: similar demand for cached context produces different hit rates because the cached contents differ.' — measured as 0.26-0.37 after collapse against 0.81-0.93 in no-surge runs at the same working set $W = 1.6$-$1.7\,C$ ($C$ the cache capacity). Abstract (fetched 2026-11-09): 'Once the cache collapses, low-reuse departure capacity sets the scale of the load reduction needed for recovery.' The model 'uses the real-system hit-rate curve in Fig. 6b' (sec. 5.1), one curve in $W/C$. KVSET 2609.27746 (fetched abstract) plans capacity from LRU stack distances with no order term.
if_true: The hit rate is a property of the dispatch protocol at fixed demand; working-set planners (KVSET, EfficientAgent 2609.33762) add a phase-dispersion term beside capacity; the recovery lever in a trap is a scheduling flag under backlog, not shedding; the sustainable session count at a given cache is up to about $1.9\times$ higher under dispersed phases than under first-come-first-served; the RL rollout collapses (MISA-T 92.4% to 4.5%; TideRL about 12%, from the killed CL-W43-12's report) are re-read as queue effects that pacing could fix without lowering concurrency.
if_false: One curve in $W/C$: the paper's account holds, order control is not a recovery lever, the stack-distance planners are complete as they stand, and the negative result is a footnote for prefix-cached agent serving.
probes: C-W45-10 (step 0 $0, 0 GPU-h, 2 d: an LRU stack-distance replay of recorded coding-agent call orders at $W/C \in \{1.2, 1.4, 1.6, 2.0\}$ under three orders; step 1 about 65 GPU-h, about $200, 8 d: the +100% ten-minute trap reproduced on an H100 pair in SGLang, then five arms x two repeats at surge end — nothing, one-shot phase jitter, random dispatch order, resident-first order, the paper's arrival cut) — cheapest
source: lifted from C-W45-10 (card 2611.02543, operators 6, 4, 7); the L3 top-down pass from the card's information_asymmetry (4) ('the engine's cached contents, not the working set, decide the hit rate after a collapse ... no exported metric names it') converged on the same mechanism, so the record carries the bottom-up origin
relates_to: CL-W43-12 (killed: this claim re-reads its rollout collapses but does not revive it)

grading.gate0: quantities written before the measurement: for session $i$, $K_i$ is the number of other sessions that called between $i$'s two consecutive calls (the LRU stack distance in session units); $i$'s prefix is still cached iff $K_i\,c < C$, with $c$ the context per session; the two branches $$h_{\mathrm{lockstep}}(W/C) = \mathbb{1}\!\left[\tfrac{W}{C} \le 1\right], \qquad h_{\mathrm{dispersed}}(W/C) = \min\!\left(1, \tfrac{C}{W}\right),$$ with $W = N c$ the working set of $N$ sessions. The dispersed formula assumes exponential inter-call times and equal contexts; step 0 replaces both with the recorded distributions. No model sampling (recorded output lengths, content discarded), so no party has a temperature; $K_i$ is read from gateway timestamps and the hit rate from the engine's cached-token counter, not from the formula; goodput is the card's definition with both thresholds visible
grading.gate1: pass: step 0 at $0, step 1 about 65 GPU-h and $200; kill written: step 0 dead if the dispersed-phase replay also predicts a hit rate below 0.4 at the trapped $W/C$ the hardware run reaches; step 1 dead if the jitter, random-order and resident-first arms each leave the hit rate below 0.45 and goodput within 20% of the untreated arm while the arrival cut recovers to within 20% of pre-surge goodput
grading.gate2: route A: the paper states the hysteresis as a fact and attributes it to contents while its model has no state for order; EfficientAgent 2609.33762 writes the dispersed-phase working set in words ('an agent's prefix is reused only if the host tier holds the reusable context of the whole agent pool'); SGLang ships `schedule_policy = 'fcfs'` and switches longest-prefix-match off above 128 waiting requests (source fetched 2026-11-09) — three source types; route B: the ruler $K_i$ with a pre-registered surprise (two branches by phase dispersion against the field's one curve; expected, judgment 0.55: the trapped state has median $K_i/(N-1)$ above 0.9 and the healthy branch below 0.6 at the same $W/C$)
grading.gate3: consumers with actions: SGLang and vLLM maintainers (the prefill scheduling default under backlog), gateway builders (Basin, Continuum, ThunderAgent — ordering before admission), KV working-set planners (an order term), RL-infra teams (MISA-T, TideRL, VenusRL — pace rather than cap concurrency). grading.gate4: mechanism: under a saturated first-come-first-served prefill queue every returning session waits behind every other, so $K_i = N - 1$ for all calls and the cache carries nothing past $W = C$; dispersed phases give $K_i \approx N(1 - e^{-\tau})$ ($\tau$ the session's inter-call time in units of its mean) and a hit rate near $C/W$; consequence: a dispatch-order flag under backlog, or admission as the paper has it

neighbors.trick: Idealize the trapped engine as a fluid FIFO server where every turn misses and rejoins the tail, prove a linear renewal recursion along FIFO orbits with a Perron root fixing gap growth, backlog and turn mix, and rescue established traps on SGLang and vLLM with a session cap at the same load.
neighbors.difference: none — occupied: the FIFO orbit is the convoy; Proposition 6 proves request-level FCFS makes reuse vanish in congestion whatever the eviction rule (scope excludes a pure resident-first order); App. E.8 ran the resident-first arm (LPM with the 128-request fallback off) in an established trap: token hit fraction 0.42-0.59 vs 0.000, no recovery by the registered rule; left open in their words: random order / jitter, ordering vs LRU touch

neighbors.title: When Cache Pressure Becomes a Trap: Metastability in Agent Serving (the card)
neighbors.trick: Count tool-idle sessions' context as prefix-cache demand; past about 1.9 C misses lengthen sessions and sessions enlarge the working set so a finite surge traps the engine; Basin admits by predicted peak context, orders by arrival plus size, lends decode memory and sheds.
neighbors.difference: occupies the trap, the fluid model, simulated cache hysteresis, and the ordering lever (sec. 5.3 resident-first as entry control; sec. 7.9 ablation: goodput 0.31-0.34 without engine priority under GPU-only caching); does not run order alone on a trapped engine; attributes the deficit to contents

neighbors.title: Multi-Turn LLM Conversations under the Least-Recently-Used Policy: Mean-Field Asymptotics and Hit Ratio Approximation
neighbors.trick: Tagged-conversation displacement process under LRU; closed-form hit ratio limit as arrival rate and capacity scale together; estimator validated on Qwen3-8B.
neighbors.difference: the dispersed branch in print under Assumption B.4 (i.i.d. inter-turn gaps); names the queue-coupled regime as excluded ('E2E latency may then substantially affect the observed prompt interarrival times')

neighbors.title: RR-Evict: Fine-Grained Prefix Cache Eviction beyond LRU for Agentic LLM Serving
neighbors.trick: Evict a tail chunk from each idle agent in round-robin order so every returning agent keeps a partial prefix.
neighbors.difference: assumes desynchronized agent phases and gives the C/W-type retained fraction deterministically from the eviction side, order-independent; its own caveat: bursts in the instantaneous active set not captured

neighbors.title: EfficientAgent: What Makes KV Cache Offloading Work for Concurrent Agents?
neighbors.trick: Size the host KV tier to the reuse working set estimated with a stack-distance model from agent histories.
neighbors.difference: states the whole-pool reuse distance for a fixed agent pool as a fact; no order term, no open arrivals

neighbors.title: The KV Cache Working Set: Online Capacity Planning for LLM Inference Systems (KVSET)
neighbors.trick: Online LRU stack distances of KV pages via the Mattson stack algorithm to read hit rate at every capacity at once.
neighbors.difference: the instrument, capacity-only; no phase or order term

kill_search.residue_headline: In an established prefix-cache trap at unchanged arrivals, SGLang's random dispatch order — which carries no prefix information — raises the token hit fraction from 0.00 to at least 0.30, so the non-collapse under LPM without its fallback (2611.08902 App. E.8, 0.42-0.59) is desynchronization and not the LRU touch of prefix matching (footnote-shaped; not a claim).
probe_consequences: C-W45-10: killed-with-claim (step 0 re-derives Proposition 6 plus Yao et al.'s estimator; arm (d) is 2611.08902 App. E.8; arm (e) is the card's sec. 5.2 and 2611.08902's CUT/SHED; arms (b) and (c) are the footnote residue, to be run on the occupants' protocol if at all)
C-W45-11: survives (orphan; not under this claim; unchanged)
kill_search.summary: Killed at the concept level (Gate 6 occupied; Gate 2B). The closest paper is Valse and Jannesari, Inside the Trap (2611.08902, 2026-11-06): it idealizes the trapped engine as a fluid FIFO server on which every turn misses and rejoins the tail of the queue — the convoy — proves that 'request-level FCFS makes reuse vanish in congestion whatever the online eviction rule' (Proposition 6, which 'covers SGLang's stock LPM through its 128-request fallback, but not a pure resident-first order'), reads the trap as a stack-distance effect ('Turn latency, not tool time, carries the gap past $R_M$'), and in App. E.8 ran the claim's resident-first arm in an established trap at unchanged arrivals: 'LPM without the fallback did not collapse: its token hit fraction over the evaluation window was 0.59 and 0.42, against 0.000', but 'It is not a fix: no run recovered by the registered rule' and 'the test does not say which of the two [ordering or LRU touch] prevents the collapse'. Its limitation text: 'Model F is an idealization: it assumes that every turn misses, that requests complete in FIFO order and that a finished turn rejoins at once'; 'Engines are colocated, with one GPU each, dense 7–8B models and pools of 150k to 956k tokens; disaggregated serving, offloading, larger models and parallelism are untested.' The second closest is the card itself (2611.02543): its hysteresis number is simulated ('the simulated hit rate remains at 0.26–0.37 after collapse'), it explains resident-first ordering as entry control ('Under resident-first scheduling, new sessions enter using the service capacity left after resident calls') and isolates the ordering lever in simulation ('To isolate engine ordering, we keep predicted admission but remove the priority from both engine queues: goodput falls to 0.81–0.95 with the host tier, 0.31–0.34 with GPU-only caching, 0.36 during recovery'); its limitation: 'All hardware experiments serve the hybrid MoE model Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on SGLang.' The dispersed branch is Yao et al. 2609.02027 under i.i.d. inter-turn gaps, which names the queue-coupled regime as excluded. The residue is a footnote: the random-dispatch arm that would separate desynchronization from LPM's LRU touch, a one-day job on the occupants' harness.

headline: Top-$k$ retrieval logs cannot price a memory but can rank one against another, and ranking is all a fixed-size memory store ever does with the price: the expected effect of every same-size swap (replacing one retrieved memory by another at the same $k$) is orthogonal to the kernel that fixed size creates (the directions in value space the log cannot see — a two-line identity), and on the card's own pooled HotpotQA log at least one pairwise contrast (a difference of two memory values) in five among memories retrieved five or more times is determined where one memory value in a thousand is.
current_belief: 2611.03289 abstract (fetched 2026-11-09): 'we prove that top-$k$ retrieval leaves every memory value undetermined, however many episodes are logged'; its remedy LEDGER 'retrieves so that the next log determines more' at 'a cost of 2.6 accuracy points on HotpotQA'; the card's information_asymmetry quotes the paper: 'the history fixes only the differences between values'. CMP 2610.02070 abstract (fetched): 'identified memory utility alone is insufficient for retention decisions'. RoMeRL, Memory-R2 and FadeMem score or learn per-memory values from fixed-size logs as if levels mattered (card neighbours).
if_true: Memory systems keep top-$k$ and lose nothing a retention, merge or retrieval policy can use; the proposed 'fraction of values determined' column becomes the fraction of contrasts determined, or is dropped; LEDGER's 2.6-point price is paid only when the store-size decision is on the table, which is when $k$ varies and the level is identified anyway; for RL memory agents the rewards fix the within-group contrasts GRPO-style objectives use, so the card's 'fixed by the learner and not by the rewards' applies to the level only.
if_false: The kernel under real top-$k$ logs is wide (aliasing of always-co-retrieved pairs, private stores), contrasts are undetermined too, and LEDGER's remedy is necessary for ranking, not only for pricing; or the LEDGER-value ranking retains a better store by at least 3 accuracy points, and the level bought something a store can act on.
probes: C-W45-12 (step 0 $0-10, 2 d: the orthogonality proof for all $|B| < d$ and the kernel of the regenerated plain top-$k$ log at $k = 5$, $T = 7{,}200$, on the card's public setup; step 1 about $20, 3 d: the retention test the card left incomplete — five rankings, keep 30% of the 2,971-memory store, 300 held-out questions, paired per question; 0 GPU-h) — cheapest
source: lifted from C-W45-12 (card 2611.03289, operators 7, 4, 5, 6): the identifiability result read against the decision space (estimable functions and contrasts, Scheffé 1959; the policy estimand projecting out the kernel, Swaminathan et al. 2016)
relates_to: CL-W44-06 (the card's theory confirms its paired-replay method)

grading.gate0: the identity before the estimator: with $(\mathbf{x}_S)_B = \mathbb{1}[B \subseteq S]$ the design row of a retrieved set $S$ and Theorem 1's kernel vectors $\mathbf{h}_B = \sum_{j \notin B} \mathbf{e}_{B \cup \{j\}} - (k - |B|)\,\mathbf{e}_B$ for $|B| < d$ ($d$ the dividend resolution), $$(\mathbf{x}_{S'} - \mathbf{x}_{S})^{\top}\mathbf{h}_B = 0 \quad \text{for every } |B| < d \text{ and every } |S'| = |S| = k.$$ The determined-contrast fraction $F_{\mathrm{pair}}$ is a function of the log's design matrix alone, computed before any outcome is read (the card's kernel test with $\tau = 10^{-8}$); the contrast statement about Shapley values is a $d = 1$ statement, the resolution of every real-data number in the card; aliasing vectors $\mathbf{e}_{\{i\}} - \mathbf{e}_{\{j\}}$ and private-store kernels are not created by fixed size and do void swaps between the aliased pair — $F_{\mathrm{pair}}$ measures how much of the real kernel is $\mathbf{h}_\emptyset$ and how much is these; the reader runs at temperature 0 (zero decision variance by construction) in one launch window, paired per question
grading.gate1: pass: about $30, 0 GPU-h, 5 days; kill written: $F_{\mathrm{pair}}$ under plain top-$k$ below 0.20 while LEDGER's size-varying log gives above 0.60 among the same memories; second kill: the LEDGER-value ranking beats the top-$k$ contrast ranking in retention by at least 3 points with the paired interval excluding zero; pre-registered uninformative reading: all five rankings within 2 points of random at 30% retention voids the retention clause (CMP's finding) while the kernel clause stands or falls on $F_{\mathrm{pair}}$ alone
grading.gate2: route B: the ruler (fraction of pairwise contrasts determined) is computable from any deployed retrieval trace with no outcomes; pre-registered surprise — expected (judgment 0.6) $F_{\mathrm{pair}} \geq 0.6$ against the card's 0.001 for levels; the field assumes the undetermined direction matters (the card's remedy and reporting proposal; RoMeRL's and Memory-R2's learned values); nobody in the fetched set says it is decision-irrelevant
grading.gate3: consumers with actions: memory-system builders (keep top-$k$; drop level-identifying retrieval), memory-benchmark owners (report contrasts determined, or nothing), RL memory-agent authors (read 'fixed by the learner' as a level statement only). One community (agent memory) — proper-shaped, with a general statement (identifiability judged against the decision space) as the ceiling
grading.gate4: mechanism: fixed $k$ confounds the intercept with the sum of values (Scheffé's one-way layout: only contrasts are estimable), and every decision a store makes is a same-size swap whose expected effect is a contrast; consequence: keep top-$k$, or LEDGER's rule is needed for ranking too
grading.gate5: durable: an identity about designs, independent of model, benchmark or memory recipe; lab-adjacent (the card's authors are the natural reviewers and could answer in a v2 — race flag)
grading.gate6: unmeasured: kill search owed (role words: estimable functions, contrasts, identifiability, positivity, Shapley, retention, memory utility, off-policy, slate). Nearest: CMP 2610.02070 (fetched; retention from the positivity side; 'no aggregation available to a retention policy predicts a memory's value on unseen queries'), 2611.03930 (paired with/without-memory design), 1605.04812 Swaminathan et al. (the kernel projected out for the policy estimand — the pre-window precedent for decision-space identifiability), Scheffé 1959 ch. 1-2 and Rao 1973 (estimable functions). Three identifiability-of-memory-utility papers in five weeks make the window short
grading.failing_gate: Gate 0 (uncounted premise: the rank bound), then Gate 2B (surprise equals the field's stated knowledge) and Gate 6 (occupied by 2610.02070 and the card's own text)
grading.rank_reason_w45: a theorem plus a $30 measurement that reverses a published remedy; one community; short window; ranked below CL-W45-08 because the gauge claim changes every compaction evaluation's protocol while this changes one remedy
grading.kill_verdict_w45: headline quantifier impossible on the named log (rank bound: <= 300 distinct rows); the qualitative clause is textbook estimable-function theory already stated by the card and by Swaminathan 2017 / 2309.15560 (Gate 2B); the decision estimand and the retention negative are CMP 2610.02070's (Gate 6)

scorecard.target_value: In print: the card leaves the decision consequence open ('the pre-registered real-data retention test was not completed.', F.7; 'Finding at query time the questions where spreading retrieval costs nothing is the open problem that remains.', sec. 6) and its synthetic retention test ranks the true levels below the reward average (5.52 against 7.14 of 300, F.7); CMP 2610.02070 states the retention gap from the other side. impact_ceiling.floor: A short note: the fixed-size kernel is orthogonal to every same-size swap, with the fraction of contrasts determined on the card's public setup and the completed retention test; cited as the reply to LEDGER; needs steps 0 and 1. Judgment p 0.55.

Judgment p 0.25.
impact_ceiling.ceiling: The general statement — identifiability is judged against the decision space, not the parameter space — adopted for tools, retrieval-augmented passages and slates, the card's own named extensions. Judgment p 0.1.

scorecard.relevance: Narasimhan (self-evolving agents, memory): direct — what a memory log can teach a learner. HAL and evaluators: moderate (a benchmark column). Systems route and L5: zero. Industry (memory-system vendors): direct. scorecard.density_and_ownership: Occupied by the card: the estimability framing, Theorem 1's kernel at every $T$, Proposition 2 (a private store asked once determines at most one value), the 55-configuration audit, LEDGER and its numbers, the reporting proposal. CMP 2610.02070 owns the positivity-side identification and the retention negative; 2611.03930 the paired design; RoMeRL and Memory-R2 the learned utilities; 1605.04812 the off-policy precedent; Scheffé and Rao the estimable-function theory. Nobody in the fetched set states that the undetermined direction is decision-irrelevant or computes a determined-contrast fraction. Density counted at the kill search in the role words above.
scorecard.why_now: The card (2026-11-02) names the kernel and leaves the decision question open in its own words with an incomplete retention test; CMP (v3 2026-10-01) states the retention gap; 2611.03930 (2026-11-02) makes three identifiability-of-memory-utility papers in five weeks; the card's public setup (pooled HotpotQA, 2,971 memories, 7,200 episodes, a hosted reader at temperature 0) makes the computation a $30 job. The identity itself is Scheffé-era, recorded as the flag.
scorecard.register_and_not: A theorem with a measurement and a recipe consequence (keep top-$k$; report contrasts). It is not a new memory system, not a retrieval rule, not a Shapley estimator, and not a claim that memory values are unimportant: it says which component of them a store ever reads.
