neighbors.title: Top-k Retrieval Leaves Memory Value Undetermined (the card)
neighbors.trick: Read the retrieval log as a linear design and test each memory's value for estimability from the retrieval counts alone; fixed size, private stores and co-retrieval each put a named vector in the kernel.
neighbors.difference: none for the identity clause — occupied by the card itself: 'the history fixes only the differences between values' (sec. 1) and slate OPE 'sets the undetermined part aside, because it does not change the value of a policy' (H.1); it does not compute a contrast fraction (bounded here at <= 45,150 / C(N,2) on its own log) and left the real-data retention test 'not completed'.

neighbors.title: Causal Memory Policy: Making Memory Utility Identifiable by Intervening on Retrieval
neighbors.trick: Reserve a fixed number of context slots for memories sampled with known propensities and estimate each memory's utility as the outcome difference between inserting it (displacing the lowest-ranked) and removing it (filling with the next-ranked) at fixed |R|.
neighbors.difference: none for the decision clause — occupied: Proposition 1 defines utility as the same-size swap ('so that |R| remains fixed across both arms'); its negative is the retention clause reversed ('none improves on retaining everything'; 'Identification does not deliver a retention policy').

neighbors.title: Off-policy evaluation for slate recommendation (Swaminathan et al. 2017, pre-window)
neighbors.trick: Estimate a slate policy's value from logged slates under additive per-slot rewards by a pseudoinverse that projects the unidentified part out.
neighbors.difference: pre-window precedent for the decision-irrelevance of the fixed-size kernel: 'the all-ones-vector 1 is in the null space of V because, for any valid slate s, we have 1_s^T 1 = l'; Lemma 2 projects the null space out and the value of every supported slate is unchanged.

neighbors.title: Identifiability Matters: Revealing the Hidden Recoverable Condition in Unbiased Learning to Rank (pre-window)
neighbors.trick: Call a click-log relevance model identifiable when relevance is recovered up to a scale, show this holds iff an identifiability graph built from the data is connected, and repair disconnected data by node intervention or merging.
neighbors.difference: the claim's structure in another field: 'identifiable up to a scaling transformation, which is sufficient for pairwise ranking objectives'; graph connectivity is the card's blocks; multiplicative nuisance on clicks, no memory.

neighbors.title: What Is This Memory Useful For? Measuring Task-Conditioned Utility in Long-Term Agent Memory
neighbors.trick: A task-blind writer stores a memory; a frozen reader answers a later task with and without it over identical filler; the paired gain is the memory's task-conditioned utility.
neighbors.difference: a designed same-size contrast ('Both arms place the same controlled filler ... and the with arm adds m'; 'Raw retains its advantage at a fixed total context'); 'We make no claim about ... a trained retention policy.' Designed, not logged; no estimability statement.

neighbors.title: Top-k Combinatorial Bandits with Full-Bandit Feedback (Rejwan & Mansour 2019, pre-window)
neighbors.trick: With only the sum of k arms' rewards observed, sample the two halves of each Hadamard row (two size-k sets), difference them, and invert the Hadamard matrix to recover every arm's mean.
neighbors.difference: its rows i != 1 are same-size swap contrasts; levels are recovered only because the model has no baseline (E[mu_S] = sum_{i in S} theta_i); with the card's theta_empty the sum row is lost and exactly the contrasts remain. Bandit, designed sampling, no memory.

neighbors.title: What Eviction Destroys: A Restore-Counterfactual Audit of Forgetting in Agent Memory
neighbors.trick: Reinstate the question's gold evidence at read time, rerun the reader, and classify each error as recoverable, irreversible or residual across four eviction policies and three budgets.
neighbors.difference: the retention-policy comparison the claim's step 1 proposes, already run on LongMemEval-S with a null ('no difference in irreversible rate among accuracy-matched policy pairs at a resolution of 1.2-6 percentage points').

neighbors.title: Reliable Memory from Unstable Growth: Curating Self-Written Agent Playbooks with Randomized Experiments
neighbors.trick: Include or exclude blocks of lessons at random on practice tasks and keep the blocks whose success gap is positive.
neighbors.difference: designed random inclusion identifies levels by construction; a curation rule, no log analysis.

neighbors.title: What Should an Agent Remember? Disentangling Retention from Retrieval in Bounded-Memory Evaluation
neighbors.trick: Cross retention rules with selection rules on the same 300 seeded episodes and hold access fixed.
neighbors.difference: 'all 319 observed failures in the bounded recency condition are caused by eviction rather than ranking errors'; separates retention from ranking, which the claim conflates.

neighbors.title: Effect Aliasing in Observational Studies (Rosenbaum & Zubizarreta 2024, pre-window)
neighbors.trick: Theory of aliasing: contrasts balanced on low-order interactions are necessarily unbalanced on high-order ones.
neighbors.difference: the card's 'aliasing' source; which contrasts are identified is a property of the design.

neighbors.title: Using graphs to find the best block designs (Bailey & Cameron 2011, pre-window)
neighbors.trick: Read a block design as its concurrence graph; estimability and optimality of treatment contrasts follow from the graph's Laplacian.
neighbors.difference: the textbook object behind F_pair: contrasts are estimable within connected components; the card's blocks are these components.

neighbors.title: Adaptive Combinatorial Experimental Design: Pareto Optimality for Decision-Making and Inference
neighbors.trick: Trade regret against statistical power in combinatorial bandits under full- and semi-bandit feedback, targeting arm gaps.
neighbors.difference: arm gaps (contrasts) as the inference target under sum feedback; designed adaptive sampling, no memory.

neighbors.title: RoMeRL
neighbors.trick: Learn per-memory utilities from outcome rewards over co-retrieved sets in a fixed-dimensional per-task state.
neighbors.difference: the learned values the claim says are read as levels; no estimability statement.

neighbors.title: Memory-R2
neighbors.trick: Rerollout memory operations from the same intermediate memory state so GRPO-style comparisons are fair.
neighbors.difference: local rerollouts are same-state contrasts; no estimability statement.

neighbors.title: MemLens
neighbors.trick: Compute Shapley-style memory values on chosen coalitions and drive retention and a dashboard from them.
neighbors.difference: replay-based valuation; the card's H.1: 'Shapley methods avoid [the question] by replaying sets'.

neighbors.title: Dual-Grained Agent Memory and Shapley Context Attribution
neighbors.trick: Decompose correctness over the retrieved rule set by Shapley attribution and re-weight retrieval by per-rule utility.
neighbors.difference: replay-based attribution used for retrieval re-weighting; no passive-log estimability.

kill_search.summary: Killed. The headline's quantifier ('at least one pairwise contrast in five is determined on the card's HotpotQA log') is impossible before any reader call: the plain top-k log is 300 questions x 24 passes with a deterministic retriever, so the design has at most 300 distinct rows and at most C(301,2) = 45,150 estimable pairs, below one in five once more than 672 memories are retrieved (the log retrieves well over 1,000; a synthetic check gives a bound of 0.04-0.07 and a sampled F_pair of 0.0000), while LEDGER's side is >= 0.797^2 = 0.635 by the card's own fraction — the probe's first kill fires at step 0. The qualitative clause is textbook: the fixed-k design is the one-way layout with k ones per row, in which no level but every contrast is estimable (Scheffé 1959, Searle 1971, Rao 1973 §4a), and the card says it on page one — 2611.03289, trick: read the retrieval log as a linear design and test each memory's value for estimability from retrieval counts alone; limitation text: 'the history fixes only the differences between values'; 'Slate off-policy evaluation works with the same counts and sets the undetermined part aside, because it does not change the value of a policy'; 'the pre-registered real-data retention test was not completed.' The decision clause is occupied by Causal Memory Policy 2610.02070, trick: reserve randomized context slots and estimate each memory's utility as the outcome difference between inserting it and removing it at fixed |R|; limitation text: 'Identification does not deliver a retention policy. CMP produces an identified measurement of per-query memory utility, and we show that this quantity does not by itself determine what to retain.' and 'Section 4 evaluates all three and none improves on retaining everything.' Pre-window precedents: Swaminathan 2017 ('the all-ones-vector 1 is in the null space of V'), 2309.15560 ('identifiable up to a scaling transformation, which is sufficient for pairwise ranking objectives'), Rejwan–Mansour 2019. Solo and lab both killed; residue is a $20 service (the incomplete retention test) with CMP's negative as the expected result.

headline: A compaction compressor (the model call that summarises an agent's own history to fit its context) at its deployed sampling setting is a gauge, not a function of the history: re-compacting the same pre-compaction history accounts for at least one tenth of the variance of post-compaction harm (TRACE's burden: errored or repeated calls among the next actions), so the one-summary-per-boundary labels the lane builds on — TRACE's paired replay, SJC's 83% entry attribution, the corpus study's history-based triggers — are single readings of an instrument whose repeatability has never been measured.
current_belief: 2610.08722 abstract (fetched 2026-11-09): the best trigger 'reaches held-out AUROC 0.66 (0.64 on the replicate's own label) against a same-boundary replicate of 0.72' — a replicate that, per its App. F (read in full by the import), splits 'each boundary's PRE and POST rollouts into disjoint halves' with the summary held fixed, so it measures the successor stage only; its authors write that 'the same numbers also support an attenuation reading' without a stage split. 2605.23296 abstract (fetched): 'the information it retains fluctuate[s] substantially from run to run, making the agent's retained knowledge unpredictable across runs' — a serving observation with no harm measurement. TRACE, SJC, HSC-Bench and 2611.06545 each use one summary per boundary.
if_true: Compaction evaluations add a writer-replicate arm ($m \geq 3$ re-compactions per boundary) beside the successor replicate and report the nested variance components; per-boundary harm labels and SJC's per-entry attribution are read as one draw; history-based triggers are read against the reliability ceiling $\rho_1 = \sigma^2_B / (\sigma^2_B + \sigma^2_W + \sigma^2_E / n)$ ($n$ continuations per summary; symbols defined in gate0); CL-W44-06's census and deletion arms average over writer draws; harness teams run the compressor at temperature 0 or ensemble $m$ draws if the share is high.
if_false: The compressor is effectively deterministic at the deployed setting (writer share under 0.10), single-summary labels are licensed, TRACE's successor-only replicate is the right yardstick, and the result is a protocol footnote; if the per-writer unsupported-policy rate is stable across re-compactions it is a calibratable writer bias (a column per writer model), not dice.

source: lifted from import S3xF9 (metrology's gauge study carried into L4; stage 7, 2026-11-08); the claim one level narrower than the occupant's limitation sentence (2610.08722: 'the same numbers also support an attenuation reading')
relates_to: CL-W44-06 (its census must average over writer draws if this holds)

grading.gate0: nested model written first: $y_{bjk} = \mu + \alpha_b + \beta_{j(b)} + \epsilon_{k(bj)}$ for boundary $b$, re-compaction $j$ and continuation $k$, with variance components $\sigma^2_B$ (between histories), $\sigma^2_W$ (writer: between summaries of one history) and $\sigma^2_E$ (successor: between continuations of one summary); the headline quantity is the writer share $\sigma^2_W / (\sigma^2_B + \sigma^2_W + \sigma^2_E)$. Whose temperature: the writer's is stated (Qwen3-8B at 0.6, gpt-oss-20b at 1.0, the developers' settings) and a temperature-0 control arm separates sampling variance from serving nondeterminism; harm is judge-free (TRACE burden; 2611.06545's ledger-checked unsupported action); the replay certificate of 2611.05650 is required — dead as a ruler if fewer than 100 of 150 snapshots re-execute to an identical state
grading.gate1: pass: about 30 GPU-h and $100, 10 days; kill written: writer share under 0.10 with the bootstrap interval's upper end under 0.20 on both writers
grading.gate2: route B: a ruler (the nested components and the reliability ceiling) with a pre-registered surprise — expected (judgment 0.45) a writer share of at least 0.25, 0.3 that it lies between 0.10 and 0.25, 0.25 that it is under 0.10 — against the field's one-summary-per-boundary practice; the corpus study's own authors name the attenuation reading and do not split the stages
grading.gate3: consumers with actions: compaction evaluators and corpus builders (TRACE 2608.06503, the corpus study 2610.08722, HSC-Bench, 2611.06545 — add the writer-replicate arm; ship summary text), gate and trigger builders (SJC 2610.20927, ACON, CL-W44-06's deletion arms — average over draws), harness and product teams (set the compressor's temperature or ensemble draws), failure-attribution standard authors (2611.05650 — a second certificate). Every compaction evaluation must change its protocol if true — community-wide within the lane

neighbors.title: Towards Reliable Context Compression for Long-Horizon Agents: An Empirical Study of Execution Instability (TRACE; v1 2026-08-06, v2 2026-10-14)
neighbors.trick: At each compaction boundary restore the environment, continue once from the full history and once from the summary, count blocked or repeated calls in the next five actions, and use the paired difference to rank summaries and rewrite the compression prompt.
neighbors.difference: Its Eq. 5 is the writer-stage re-draw: the same compressor and prompt produce three summaries of one history, each with its own POST continuations and shared PRE; the best-worst spread is the training signal. It reports no variance component; its 590-boundary cohort has one summary per boundary; compressor temperature unstated (Ollama).

neighbors.title: Compact-Bench: Measuring What Context Compaction Costs Long-Horizon Coding Agents (v2 2026-10-22)
neighbors.trick: Continue 35 SWE-bench repairs from one cached history and snapshot with the full history and with each of 14 summarizers' summaries; a repair is damaged when PRE passes and POST fails.
neighbors.difference: A joint writer-plus-successor re-draw on every damaged cell: summary and POST resampled over three seeds, PRE reused; 120 of 126 first-round damages recur (stable damage), 6 are seed variance. Not split by stage, conditioned on first-round damage, service-default temperature, no variance component.

neighbors.title: Parallel Context Compaction for Long-Horizon LLM Agent Serving (2026-05-22)
neighbors.trick: Compact a long history in parallel blocks instead of one blocking call so the operator controls summary volume and latency.
neighbors.difference: The summary-level gauge study: ten re-compactions of an identical snapshot and prompt; length CV 16-85% and pairwise cosine 0.47-0.86 across backbones and 4k-96k inputs; the claim's mechanism sentence is in its Section 5.2. No continuation, no harm, no stage partition.

neighbors.title: Does an Agent's History Tell You When Compaction Will Hurt? A Modest, Bounded Effect on the TRACE Paired-Replay Corpus (2026-10-06)
neighbors.trick: On 590 replayed boundaries, train triggers to predict harm from the pre-boundary history and compare them with a split-half replicate of the same boundary's rollouts (AUROC 0.66 vs 0.72).

neighbors.title: Adapting Context Compression for Long-Horizon Agents with Counterfactual Continuations (PAIR; 2026-09-29; TRACE's group)
neighbors.trick: Restore the state at each realized compaction, continue to termination from the full and the compressed context m times, and define the boundary's hazard and burden as the difference of expected outcomes.
neighbors.difference: Writes the compressor as a distribution (c ~ C(. | x, B), 'Stochastic context compressor') and the effect as a function of the realized draw; evaluates one realized summary per boundary with m continuations.
